newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr up on short-covering, Sakakibara by Tokyo noon.
newsitem.headline: Dlr up on short-covering, Sakakibara by Tokyo noon.

text.p: 0314 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0300 GMT
The dollar rose by noon on Thursday on short-covering by overseas funds and interbank dealers after falling to 7-month low of 110.62 yen overnight.

The greenback started rising towards 113 yen in the late morning after senior Ministry of Finance (MOF) official Eisuke Sakakibara said an excessive strengthening of the yen is undesirable, dealers said.

"I don't think there is a feeling in the market that a downward test is over. But Japanese investors and trust banks, who had sold dollars in the past few days, started buying back the greenback," a city bank dealer said.
Another city bank dealer said: "The dollar was bought against the yen following Sakakibara's comment."

Traders had already started buying back dollars in early trade as they had speculated Sakakibara would not make yen-supportive comments after the dollar dropped sharply against the yen in the past few days, dealers said.
The dollar rose as high as 112.90 yen by midday.
After attending a financial seminar in Tokyo, Sakakibara told reporters that Japan will deal decisively against excessive moves in the foreign exchange market.
He added that he does not think Japan's trade surplus will be a major issue at the summit meeting of the Group of Seven industrial nations in Denver on June 20-22.
He also said Japan does not think the country's trade surplus will expand greatly.
Meanwhile, Sakakibara was quoted as saying that an imminent rate rise was unlikely.
After his comments, the dollar rose above 113 yen.
